branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو اليسار بمعنى الغنى ولا اليسار خلاف اليمين.

root_profile.summary: Kök, kolaylık ve hazır oluş çevresindeki merkezden azlık, maddi bolluk, sol yön, uyumlu hareket, hayvancılık, tarihsel talih oyunu, beden izleri ve teknik yönelimlere uzanan çok dallı bir anlam yapısı taşır. Yer ve kişi adları ile genç erkek anlamı daha bağımsız uçlarda yer alır.

text.arabic_uthmani: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌۭ

baseline.text: Allah'ın yaratmayı nasıl başlattığını, sonra onu nasıl tekrarladığını görmediler mi? Bu Allah'a kolaydır.

findings.text: Yaratılıştaki tekrarlanan süreçler, yeniden yaratmayı tek seferlik bir olağanüstülükten çok daha önce gösterilmiş bir gücün yeniden uygulanması olarak düşündürür.
Yeniden yaratmanın kolaylığı, işin önemsizliğini değil, ilahi işlemin hiçbir engelle durdurulamamasını anlatır.

activation_trace.role: Perception by eye or insight makes the process evidential rather than merely announced.
The explicit branch pairing of beginning with return organizes the two verbs as one recurrent process.
Return after departure and doubling after a beginning supplies the recurrence.
Ease after difficulty removes any implied obstacle to the repeated act.

changed_reading.after: A challenge to infer effortless re-origination from an observable pattern of beginning and return.
changed_reading.before: A bare assertion that God can create twice.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا ... يُبْدِئُ ... ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ... يَسِيرٌ links seeing, first production, subsequent return, and ease.
baseline_models.mechanism: The rhetorical question treats origination and return as one inspectable pattern: perception should move from a witnessed beginning to recognition that its repetition poses no obstruction to God.

activation_trace.role: Prior measurement and proportion supply an intelligible pattern for the created form.
Actual origination turns the measured pattern into created existence.
Opening and precedence mark the first realization of the pattern.
Repetition supplies re-formation rather than an unrelated second product.
The sense of smallness makes the repeated work slight relative to divine agency.

changed_reading.after: Creation is measured form-making whose already established pattern can be re-realized without strain.
changed_reading.before: Creation is an unstructured act followed by another act.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: خَلْقَ stands between initiating and redoing, while its branch inventory joins measurement to bringing into being.
baseline_models.mechanism: Creation can be read as a measured pattern before it is an produced form; once the pattern is determined and first realized, return is re-forming according to that measure, which sharpens why it is easy.

activation_trace.role: Reflective seeing invites consideration of the whole trajectory rather than one visual instant.
Firstness supplies the trajectory's origin.
Return as destination or place of return supplies the trajectory's terminus.
Ease characterizes divine command of the entire origin-to-terminus movement.

changed_reading.after: God governs creation's whole passage from first emergence to its appointed return.
changed_reading.before: God performs a first creation and later duplicates it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The firstness of يُبْدِئُ and the destination sense within يُعِيدُهُ can form an origin-to-return arc.
baseline_models.mechanism: Instead of hearing only two production events, the clause can describe creation as a trajectory: it is launched from a first point and caused to reach its return or destination.

activation_trace.role: Divine origination supplies the positive side of the agency test.
Fabricating false speech supplies a counterfeit human mode of 'creating' that the focus reverses.
A lie diverted from truth identifies the fabricated product as epistemically false.
Denied possession and disposal mark the worshipped objects' lack of effective agency.
Allocated provision supplies the concrete function the idols cannot control and God can.

changed_reading.after: The ayah also unmasks fabricated gods and claims by testing them against actual originating, sustaining, and returning agency.
changed_reading.before: The ayah only proves a second creation is possible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The Abraham unit places human fabrication of falsehood and the idols' lack of control over provision beside God's origination and return of creation. Creative agency therefore becomes a criterion that separates a manufactured object or claim from the one worthy of worship.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the lexical contrast in خ ل ق and the sequence from worship and provision to divine creation; I infer that origination is being used as a worship-eligibility test. A live alternative is that 29:19 begins an independent resurrection argument.
structural_cues: 29:16-19 moves from the command to worship God, through fabricated idols and absent provision, to the question about God's creative action.

activation_trace.role: Seeing in the focus poses the evidential task that the next ayah specifies.
Motion and travel turn observation into an active itinerary.
The lower terrestrial realm supplies the field in which evidence is to be examined.
Directed sight or insight supplies the investigative act.
The repeated beginning-plus-return branch resolves the echo with the focus.
The same created object confirms that the two ayat pursue one evidential question.
Producing and establishing something names the later act more distinctly than generic return.
Laterness explicitly locates the second genesis after the first.
Effective capability closes the inquiry by affirming power to realize its result.

changed_reading.after: Seeing is a field practice of moving through terrestrial evidence and reasoning from first emergence to a specifically later genesis.
changed_reading.before: Seeing is a general appeal to notice that creation exists.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah operationalizes 'seeing': movement through the earth and directed inspection are the method, the beginning of creation is the object, and the later genesis is the inferred horizon.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the verbal echo, terrestrial movement, directed النظر, and the later genesis; I infer that 29:20 explicates how the seeing requested in 29:19 is to occur. The weaker alternative is simple rhetorical repetition without a prescribed inquiry.
structural_cues: 29:20 nearly repeats كَيْفَ بَدَأَ ٱلْخَلْقَ after the paired imperatives to travel and inspect, then replaces the focus's pronoun with ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ.

activation_trace.role: The collective created order is the broad referent later distributed across individual selves.
Return as destination leaves open the terminus that 29:57 names.
The life-bearing self individualizes the focus's collective creation.
Experienced trial makes death an undergone transition rather than an abstraction.
Loss of life supplies the interval across which return operates.
Explicit return to God identifies both motion and destination.

changed_reading.after: Every self is personally carried through death as one instance of creation's Godward return.
changed_reading.before: The return concerns creation as an impersonal totality.

context_deltas.mechanism: The whole-surah return sequence resolves the collective object 'creation' into every living self: each personally undergoes death and then returns toward God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the parallel temporal sequence and explicit destination; I infer that every self is an instance of the creation God returns. A live alternative is that 29:57 uses return only for judgment while 29:19 concerns re-creation as a physical act.
structural_cues: 29:57 reproduces the focus's ثُمَّ sequence: every self tastes death, then 'to Us you are returned.'

activation_trace.role: Beginning paired with return provides the abstract cycle instantiated by the later scene.
Return after departure supplies renewed life after its disappearance.
Delivered descent supplies the incoming cause in the ecological sequence.
Water conveyed by pouring or irrigation supplies the material mediator.
The branch explicitly images earth becoming alive through rain and vegetation.
Soft fertile earth supplies the receptive created substrate.
Afterness following a prior state fixes the temporal reversal.
Lifeless land or matter supplies the dead state from which visible reanimation occurs.

changed_reading.after: Rain-driven reanimation of dead earth makes return presently legible as a material and ecological process.
changed_reading.before: Return is future and unavailable to observation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Water is delivered, enters the earthly field, and produces plant-life after that field's death. This supplies a visible small-scale mechanism for the focus's movement from origination to renewed creation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet's grammar supplies divine water-delivery followed by enlivening after death; I infer that this ecological scene is a concrete analogue for يُعِيدُهُ. The alternative is that the scene concerns present provision only and does not model resurrection.
structural_cues: 29:61-63 moves from the conceded creation of heavens and earth to a second question whose stated sequence is water, earth, life, and after-death renewal.

activation_trace.role: Heart-opinion and reflection make seeing an interpretive judgment.
A remaining visible sign supplies evidence available for inspection.
Manifest disclosure characterizes the sign as clear rather than hidden.
Reason as a restraint against ignorance supplies the needed cognitive uptake.
The ruined dwellings are presented as already evident to the audience.
Making conduct appear attractive supplies the distortion applied to visible evidence.
Diversion supplies the blocked movement from perception to the right path.
Inner insight makes the failure paradoxical: perceptive capacity coexists with misdirection.

changed_reading.after: The evidence is available, but seeing fails when attraction and path-diversion prevent reflective recognition.
changed_reading.before: The addressees lack information about how creation begins and returns.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah distinguishes exposed evidence from successful understanding: a sign can remain, dwellings can be evident, and people can possess insight, yet adornment can redirect them from the path. The focus's 'have they not seen' therefore diagnoses failed uptake, not missing sensory data.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies visible evidence, claimed or possessed insight, and a blocking sequence; I infer that the focus rebukes a failure to integrate what is seen. The alternative is the simpler charge that the addressees have never observed the relevant evidence.
structural_cues: 29:35 joins a clear sign to reasoning; 29:38 joins evident dwellings and insight to adornment and diversion.

activation_trace.role: Reflective seeing demands that an admitted premise be followed to its consequence.
The audience concedes divine origination of the largest visible order.
Subjection toward a purpose adds continuing governance to original creation.
Their spoken answer makes the creator premise explicit rather than inferred by the reader.
Being turned from the proper direction supplies the failure between concession and conclusion.

changed_reading.after: The question confronts an audience that already admits divine creation but refuses to infer return and exclusive agency from it.
changed_reading.before: The question introduces evidence the audience does not know.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later questioning shows the audience already conceding that God created the heavens and earth and subjected the celestial lights. The focus's question thus exposes an inference they resist rather than soliciting an unknown premise.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the admitted creator premise and the following accusation of reversal; I infer that 29:19 targets cognitive inconsistency. A live alternative is that the later audience is rhetorically distinct from the earlier one.
structural_cues: 29:61 asks who created and subjected, records the answer 'God,' and immediately asks how they are turned away.

activation_trace.role: Repetition provides continuity between the first and later created states.
Return as destination permits the terminus to differ in quality from the point of departure.
Life as effective benefit or good sharpens the contrast between nominal present life and the later living reality.
Diversion by something else marks present life as displaced from its true object.
Action without a sound end marks the present mode as structurally unserious.
A dwelling in which states circulate supplies the setting for the contrasting later mode.
Laterness identifies the destination as subsequent to the first life.

changed_reading.after: Return preserves continuity while opening into a later mode presented as more truly alive than the first.
changed_reading.before: Re-creation simply restores the same kind of life.

context_deltas.mechanism: The current life is classified as diversion and unserious play, while the later dwelling is identified as life in an intensified sense. Return therefore need not mean restoration to an identical mode; it can culminate in a more fully operative life.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the evaluative contrast between two lives; I infer that the focus's return preserves identity without requiring qualitative sameness. The alternative is that 29:64 evaluates conduct and duration but says nothing about the mechanics of re-creation.
structural_cues: 29:64 balances this worldly life against the later dwelling and reserves the emphatic living designation for the latter.

activation_trace.role: The focus establishes the rhetorical formula of perceptible evidence.
The repeated formula supplies an internal comparison for what counts as 'seeing.'
Causing something to occupy a condition supplies the establishment of protected order.
A bounded sanctuary supplies the stable spatial form.
Security and heart-settled trust couple protected space to the epistemic response it should evoke.
Swift snatching supplies the unstable counterfield around the sanctuary.
The surrounding direction makes the protected center legible by contrast with its perimeter.

changed_reading.after: Its mode of seeing also includes recognizing maintained order through contrasts of stability and disruption in lived social space.
changed_reading.before: The focus points only to natural objects as evidence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeats the exact 'have they not seen' challenge for a protected sanctuary surrounded by human snatching. That parallel broadens evidential seeing from biological or cosmic process to stable social space maintained amid surrounding instability.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated formula and center-periphery contrast; I infer that the earlier question likewise asks for recognition of ordered maintenance, not raw eyesight alone. The alternative is that the two questions share rhetoric but not an evidential mechanism.
structural_cues: 29:19 and 29:67 share أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا; the latter immediately contrasts an established secure center with seizure around it.

remaining_uncertainties: Whether يُعِيدُهُ should remain strictly eschatological or may also carry ecological and behavioral recurrence as secondary activations.
How much interpretive weight the branch-distant split mappings and apportionment cluster can bear beyond an explicitly exploratory outlier.
Whether 29:64's intensified later life describes the quality of returned creation or only contrasts the value of two modes of conduct.
strongest_changes: 29:17 turns the focus into a creator-agency test against fabricated falsehood and powerless worshipped objects.
29:20 converts 'seeing' into terrestrial travel and inspection and names the result as the later genesis.
29:57 personalizes the returned creation as every death-bound self returning to God.
29:63 makes reanimation observable in water-mediated life of dead earth.
29:61 shows that the problem is failure to follow an admitted creator premise, not lack of that premise.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context made one compact ayah work simultaneously as a worship criterion, a method of inquiry, a personal mortality sequence, an ecological reanimation model, and an indictment of failed epistemic uptake without forcing those mechanisms into one reading.

activation_trace.role: Habit, training, and repeated action open a behavioral register within return.
A condition that revisits a person supplies recurrence of devotional states.
Circular motion supplies the scene's cyclical spatial image.
Exclusive purification from association marks the crisis-phase turn toward God.
Deliverance by separation supplies the pivot from danger to safety.
Renewed association after rescue completes the relapse cycle.

changed_reading.after: As a contained analogy, the same recurrence register exposes humans repeatedly returning to exclusive devotion in danger and back to association in safety.
changed_reading.before: Return applies only to God's second production of creatures.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it lets the return branches of يُعِيدُهُ activate a human behavioral cycle rather than the primary cosmic re-creation. It remains anchored in ع و د's habit and recurring-state branches and in the explicit crisis-rescue-relapse sequence of 29:65; downstream prose should present it only as a secondary analogy, not as a replacement sense for resurrection.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يُعِيدُهُ can activate recurrence as acquired habit or a state that comes back, alongside its primary return-of-creation sense.

activation_trace.role: A share given first supplies initial apportionment.
Measuring and proportioning supply the governing calculation of the created form.
The packet's split mapping activates enumeration as a possible image of the returning totality.
Lots and division of a carcass supply a concrete but form-distant image of apportioned shares.
Restriction to a measured amount reinforces apportionment at the level of provision.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, creation and return resemble a measured allocation whose members can be re-enumerated and reapportioned without loss.
changed_reading.before: Ease means only that repeating creation requires little effort.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading is branch-distant because it combines the initial-share branch of beginning, measurement in creation, the split ع د د mapping under return, and the lots-division branch of ease. The convergence remains focus-anchored and is lightly reinforced by measured provision in 29:62; downstream prose must call it an accounting or apportionment image activated by the branches, not claim that يُعِيدُهُ lexically means 'counts it.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus clusters branches of first allotment, measured formation, enumeration, and division by lots around the beginning-return sequence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Return as repetition of an observable operation.** ع و د B001 is “returning after departure and doing again,” with B004 adding practiced repetition. Beginning and restoring are joined by ثم and made the object of seeing “how.” I infer that recurrent processes in creation furnish an operational analogy for restoration; return reads less as an isolated marvel than as the reapplication of a displayed capacity.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 29:63's rain reviving dead earth supplies the strongest later observable instance of repeated bringing-forth. It turns the general “how” of creation into a visible death-to-life process.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Seeing should become judgment about a beginning-return process.** Lexical evidence: `يَرَوْا`, root `ر ء ي`, `B002` (opinion and reflective judgment); `يُبْدِئ`, root `ب د ء`, `B001` (beginning and initiating); `ٱلْخَلْق`, root `خ ل ق`, `B001` (measuring and proportioning); and `يُعِيدُه`, root `ع و د`, `B001` (returning and doing again). Structural cue: `ثُمَّ` orders initiation before repetition; `29:14-15` supplied destruction and preserved rescue, while `29:20` commands travel and observation. Assigned role: reflective sight infers repeatability from proportioned origination. Abductive move: the packet does not expose the hidden mechanics of return; I infer only the abductive bridge invited by the sequence: an observed capacity to initiate supports capacity to repeat. Reading change: the ayah asks for process-judgment, not passive visual notice.

2. **Ease means an unobstructed reopening, not triviality.** Lexical evidence: `يَسِير`, root `ي س ر`, `B001` (ease and ready opening). Structural cue: the preceding initiation-return pair is followed by `29:20`'s latter emergence and `29:21`'s reversal; `29:24` will show rescue through fire. Assigned role: ready opening characterizes the lack of resistance in the divine operation. Abductive move: I infer from nearby human attempts to block, kill, or escape that “easy” denies effective obstruction, not the seriousness of what is done. Reading change: return is read as a readily opened operation under divine agency.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - **Later activation (`29:63-64`):** Rain reviving earth after its death supplies the material process-image that the earlier beginning-return claim left unstated, and the next ayah names the later abode as concentrated life. The analogy strengthens repeatability without pretending ecological rain is the hidden resurrection mechanism.

words.gloss_range: interrogative hamza opening a negated seeing clause as rhetorical challenge rather than information request
words.prose: {{ar:أَ}} ({{tr:a}}) opens the ayah in challenge mode. Its question-shape is not a neutral request for information; joined to the following negative seeing clause, it presses the audience toward the answer that the evidence should already have been recognized. The tiny opening sound also makes the challenge arrive immediately, before the creation process is named.

topics.headline: interrogative form becomes evidential rebuke
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah starts by indicting failed recognition, not by asking a neutral question.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the opening as interrogative plus negative seeing force, supporting a rhetorical challenge that expects recognition.

topics.headline: single-letter launch makes the challenge abrupt

topics.reason: The particle is a single-letter interrogative attached to the following cluster, so the form-specific and audible-launch rows survive as local surface payoff.

words.gloss_range: connective waw plus jussive negative lam, linking back while negating the perception verb
words.prose: {{ar:وَلَمْ}} ({{tr:wa-lam}}) binds continuation to indictment. The connective keeps 29:19 attached to the prior messenger-duty statement (29:18), while the negative particle governs the seeing verb as a past-negated failure. The cluster therefore does two jobs at once: it carries the discourse forward and places the whole perception of origination and return under denial. It also helps the discourse step back from direct address into third-person exposure of the deniers' non-seeing.

topics.headline: lam governs the failed seeing clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the failure is grammatically governed, not a loose statement about ordinary looking.
topics.reason: QAC marks lam as a jussive negative particle governing the following perception verb, and attachment evidence makes the seen content the embedded process clause.

topics.headline: connective cluster continues the prior argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that creation evidence follows the limited messenger-duty statement (29:18) as the next public proof.
topics.reason: The waw is licensed as connective coordination; the boundary rows coherently connect this challenge to 29:18 without adding a new local parse.

topics.headline: address becomes third-person distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a rhetorical step back: the deniers are now discussed as a group whose non-seeing can be exposed.
topics.reason: The following verb carries third-person plural agreement, so the boundary row about distancing is locally coherent.

words.gloss_range: jussive perception verb: seeing that reaches recognition and judgment, governed by negation and taking an embedded manner clause as object
words.prose: {{ar:يَرَوْا}} ({{tr:yaraw}}) carries the audience's failed perception. Because it is jussive under lam, the non-seeing is grammatically marked as a past failure, while the root range makes the demanded seeing more than eye-contact: visible creation should become considered recognition. Its object is not a single noun but the kayfa clause, so what they fail to perceive is the process by which God originates and then returns creation. The same opening formula recurs in observational proof settings (21:30; 24:43; 30:50; 29:67), and the standard third-person form keeps the audience at rhetorical distance even though the variant pressure shows the challenge could confront them directly.
words.root_gloss_range: root range spans physical sight, perception, dream-vision, and considered judgment; local use selects public perception moving toward recognition

words.gloss_range: embedded manner interrogative/adverbial: how, in what mode, governing attention to the process of origination and return
words.prose: {{ar:كَيْفَ}} ({{tr:kayfa}}) turns the seeing challenge toward manner. The ayah is not asking whether creation exists or who creates; it asks them to perceive how God originates creation and then returns it. Because the embedded question covers the whole process clause, the word serves as the hinge from epistemic challenge to cosmological evidence, and it helps the ayah's larger movement from challenge, to process, to emphatic conclusion. It also answers the prior clear-delivery frame (29:18) by making creation itself the clear evidence now demanded for perception.

topics.headline: manner question makes process visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof lies in observing the mode and process of creation, not merely conceding existence.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as an embedded manner interrogative/adverbial, with translation support warning that its scope covers the process clause.

topics.headline: challenge process conclusion architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah as an argument with three beats: challenge, observed process, and verdict.
topics.reason: The clause evidence supports a main rhetorical seeing clause followed by a concluding inna-clause.

topics.headline: clear delivery is answered by clear evidence

words.gloss_range: Form IV imperfect of originating/beginning: God causes creation to begin in a present observable process
words.prose: {{ar:يُبْدِئُ}} ({{tr:yubdiʾu}}) names origination as a present, observable divine act. Its Form IV shape makes God the one who causes the beginning, while the rare root gives the first pole a marked start-point and unprecedented-origination force. The preserved final hamza keeps the beginning-root visibly and audibly marked inside the verb. The verb is not isolated: it opens a specialized origination-return pair with yuʿīduhu, a formulaic dyad also seen in creation-return passages (10:4; 21:104; 27:64; 30:11; 30:27; 85:13). The same root is immediately reopened in 29:20, so this act becomes the first movement in a two-ayah argument about beginning and final bringing forth.
words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on beginning, initiation, and unprecedented origination; local Form IV selects caused origination

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in nominative subject position: the explicit agent of origination
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) makes the agent of origination explicit. The verb already carries a recoverable masculine singular subject, but the ayah names God in nominative case between act and object, so the process is not left as an unnamed natural cycle. The proper name gives the creator-agent maximal definiteness and participates in the familiar God-creation pairing. The derivational field can leave worship, turning, and refuge pressure near the name, while the nominative subject role keeps the local function controlled. The later genitive Allāhi recasts the same name from agent of origination into the domain for ease.
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field; derivational disputes may color relational force but local grammar selects the named subject of origination

words.gloss_range: definite accusative verbal noun/object: creation as act and created order, treated as one returnable field
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْخَلْقَ}} ({{tr:al-khalqa}}) is the direct object of origination. Its definite verbal-noun form lets the ayah hold together the act of creating and the created order that results, so the audience is asked to observe both process and product. The singular collective shape compresses creation into one returnable referent, later resumed by the suffix in yuʿīduhu and then by dhālika. The root's measuring and fashioning field makes the object an ordered creation, while the fabrication branch is only a contrast: this context points to observable reality, not invented speech. In recitation, the named subject flows directly into this definite object, making the subject-object movement audible.
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes creating, fashioning, measuring, inherent constitution, and fabricating; local sense selects real measured creation while the fabrication branch survives only as contrast

topics.headline: definite accusative object of origination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that creation is the acted-upon object after the divine subject, not an independent actor.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the word as definite accusative direct object of the origination verb.

topics.headline: verbal noun holds act and result together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word can carry both creating-as-process and creation-as-result in the same object.
